So with Neurological De-Armoring, I'm fixing the underpinnings first, instead of redecorating. I use Ketones (BHB), which block HDAC (an enzyme that keeps genes switched off), along with Glutamate modulation, and together they work like a metabolic solvent to soften the "concrete" in the brainstem. That lets us dig under the house and pour a new foundation, so we can then update the psychological software upstairs.

The Anti-Breakthrough (Micro-Dosing): Dr. Perry found that for a dysregulated brain, the "therapeutic window" is often only seconds long, so a sensitized, armored nervous system just can't take in sixty minutes of trauma processing, which is why long sessions can leave you wrecked for days. So for now, we give up on the "hour-long breakthrough."

Instead, aim for Micro-Dosing Safety: 30 seconds of regulated breathing, twenty times a day. It's more like physical therapy for a broken nervous system than running a marathon, so how often you do it matters more than how hard you push.

The Signal Dial (GluD Receptors): Johns Hopkins researchers recently discovered that the brain also uses GluD receptors as a kind of master volume knob, so if NMDA is the spark, GluD sets the baseline "hum" of the synapse. In an armored state that dial often gets jammed, either on "High" (Cerebellar Ataxia/Hyper-vigilance) or on "Low" (Apathy/Schizotypy).

The Repair (Leucine/L-Serine): L-Serine is what the brain makes D-Serine from, so it can help recalibrate the GluD "Volume Dial" and make therapy sessions that end with low fear and a sense of mastery stick better. The conversion isn't very efficient though, so some people take D-serine itself instead (more risk, but also more benefit). And we use Leucine for structural repair, since it also tunes synaptic gain, which eases the "itchy brain" feeling.

The Governor (Agmatine): For the hot, itchy, reactive, pain-y, rumination-heavy kind of Glutamate Storm, agmatine is the optional "voltage governor" I'd use. It may help when the problem isn't just excess glutamate in the synapse but NMDA/GluN2B over-reactivity, so you use it as a brake while you're in that state, not every day like a foundation nutrient.

Important conflict: don't take agmatine in the same session as D-Serine/DCS-style exposure or EMDR work, since agmatine partly brakes NMDA activity, and those tools need NMDA to do the learning and memory updating they're there for. So I'd use agmatine for storm control, but not right before a session where you're deliberately working on reconsolidation.

We grew up building a "role-self" to please and manage the people around us. And the role-self psychology gets locked in physiologically by Dopamine and DeltaFosB, which also underlie addictions, so it's a vicious cycle as both create the other. That's why I built this protocol, to go after the chemistry holding the false persona in place, so the person you were before the trauma (your "True-Self") can come back out.
